A.biggest_strength: A true mechanical visual explanation: animated argument and return value 'chips' physically travel across frames and substitute into caller expressions in real time, anchored by Scene 0's unified semantic color-coding of function components across six languages simultaneously.
A.biggest_weakness: The interactive step-by-step runner directly simulates 6 languages (Python, JavaScript, Ruby, C, Java, Rust), leaving the remaining 7 languages to the comparative reference table.

B.biggest_strength: Outstanding breadth in the interactive player, allowing readers to step through code and view tailored execution notes across 14 distinct languages, including Go, Swift, C#, PHP, Haskell, and handwritten x86-64 assembly.
B.biggest_weakness: The visualization relies primarily on static HTML text boxes appearing and disappearing rather than illustrating data flow, and mobile readability suffers from horizontally overflowing tables and tightly wrapped tabs.
factual_errors: In the stack frame view, intermediate subexpression values are labeled and stored as named frame variables (e.g., 'square(a) = 9' and 'square(b) = 16' inside the sumOfSquares frame), conflating temporary evaluation registers/operand stacks with activation record local variables.

The 'How arguments are passed' table lists C++ std::move as a parameter passing style ('By move'), whereas std::move is an unconditional rvalue cast and parameters in C++ are passed either by value (invoking the move constructor) or by reference (T&&).
Step 10 announces that 'Printing is one more function call' that 'goes through the same five steps', but does not push a stack frame for the print/printf invocation.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is the clear winner because it visualizes the actual mechanism of a function call rather than simply placing text descriptions beside boxes. Its animated value chips show how arguments pass into parameters and how return values replace call expressions in the caller. Scene 0's simultaneous side-by-side view instantly imparts the universal core idea across all languages, while scenes 6 and 7 provide unmatched depth with real bytecode/assembly disassembly and empirical stack-limit measurements. Page A also excels in mobile responsiveness and accessibility with adaptive SVG viewports and full keyboard/reduced-motion support.
